text:
Controlled use may have an impact on the economic effects of ORV. Adversity would be lessened by adequate and consistent administration of ORV. In many instances, it will be offset further by enhancement of vacation land and home values and related off season influx of tourists.
In some situations, the off-road vehicle offers the user an opportunity to escape the pressures of high-density civilization and be alone or in company of like-minded individuals. Other users test their driving skills in open-country competitive events. In other cases there are individuals and families who participate in ORV activities in conjunction with other outdoor activities such as camping.
In many instances, a mixture of transportation modes and an increased number of users on the same area or trail has increased the hazard potential to the user. Many trails are not designed or constructed for vehicle use or to safely accommodate mixed use, and terrain features may create or increase hazard to a particular type of use. In the winter, avalanches can pose a threat to oversnow vehicle users. The proposed action will include the investigation of areas where traffic mixes can and cannot be safely accommodated and control use to improve safety to all users.
Users, including their followers, supporters, and suppliers, will experience a reduction in their freedom to use any public lands whenever they wish. The user will be inconvenienced in instances where closure of an area requires a longer travel distance to use his vehicle. Spectators and suppliers may object to the potential reduction of their activity. The users may benefit from having areas specifically designated and controlled in which they have relative freedom to operate their vehicles.
Most motorized ORV are noisy in excess of acceptable levels to the non-ORV user. The noise can permanently affect human hearing for users as well as other recreationists and animals who happen to be nearby. Even with mufflers and other noise reduction devices the attendant noise levels from ORV may have an impact upon animals and people using the same areas in certain circumstances. This is particularly disconcerting to many users of the public lands because it conflicts with their values of peace and quiet or with their pursuit of a harmonious relationship with nature. Reduction of noise levels in areas where permitted could reduce the non-compatibility of machine to man and animal.
In the viewpoint of many, trails, parking areas, rest stops, and other developments associated with ORV use are unsightly--particularly in relatively natural areas. Traces of the ORV, such as ruts, litter, etc., where no trails are provided are even more offensive to ORV non-users.
Designation of trails and areas where the ORV can be used should reduce the magnitude of the potential aesthetic degradation.
